transcript.text: My dream desk setup is pretty simple.

As long as the desk is nice and clean, the
clutter of gadgets is kept to a minimum, and

it’s ergonomic to support me throughout
the day.
You can’t really go wrong with the design.

Hi I’m David and here’s a quick tour of
my desk setup for 2017
So let’s start with desk top.

The IKEA Karlby in the dark walnut color is
an incredibly popular choice for desk setups
these days.

The walnut mosaic design, a nice long length,
and the relatively low price tag, it’s no
wonder why it is so popular.
And I absolutely love it.

But if you’re planning on getting one yourself,
just be aware, it’s built from a 1/8”

Walnut veneer on top of particleboard so it
won’t be as strong as a more expensive solid

wood top, the depth measures only at 65cm
deep which can be a little too short for some

monitor setups, and the Walnut wood grain
has some rough edges that can splinter or

catch on clothing fibers, so it will need
some extra maintenance to ensure it looks
pristine over time.
The next part to the desk is the legs.

I’m using an electric sit stand desk legs
from Anthrodesk.

These desk legs are solid enough to hold up
the heavy wood top, and the clean straight
lines matches well with the rest of the look.

With the fully programmable function keys
I can quickly switch between sitting and standing.

And when I combine the desk height flexibility
with my highly adjustable IKEA Volmar office

chair, and a rolled up yoga mat as a foot
rest underneath.

I’m able to setup everything just right
to make it the perfect ergonomic desk configuration
for me.

The next key part to my perfect desk ergonomics
is the computer monitor.
I’m using a Dell U3415 ultrawide monitor.

And I think this is still one of the best
quality and value ultrawide monitors available
for productivity purposes.

And when I combine it with a Vivo monitor
arm, I can position the monitor at my perfect

height, angle, and close to the back edge
of the desk which is important with the short
depth of thes karlby desk top.

And by offsetting the arm to the side I’m
also able to achieve this floating monitor

configuration that looks great with the whole
minimalistic desk design.

For me a clean desk setup means removing as
many wires as possible.

So while not the best for performance, I’m
all for wireless peripherals.

I’m using the Logitech K810 keyboard which
has a nice small footprint without the number

pad, a low profile design so I don’t really
need a palm rest, and automatic backlighting
that is convenient for sessions at night.

Also when I need to quickly charge I have
an auto retracting micro usb cable behind
my monitor so I never worry about low batteries.

And I pair the keyboard with the Logitech
G602 mouse that matches nicely in color scheme
and continues to serve me well.

And finally some low key Edifier speakers,
and a PC in the sleek small footprint Silverstone

FT03 chassis finishes off the rest of the
key components.
So that’s my dream desk setup for 2017.
A pure clean, minimal, and ergonomic setup.

While I could probably add a plant or some
new artwork down the line to add some additional
color.

I’m really pleased with the simplicity of
it all as it stands today.
But hope you guys enjoyed this one.
You know what to do.
And I’ll see you in the next video.

nodes.plm_action: Lifting the desk up
nodes.plm_caption:
An animated opening sequence for "clean minimal ergonomic" and "dream desk by david."
We see a wooden desk with a floating monitor as a man begins sitting on the other side, with a small cup, keyboard and mouse as he adjusts the desk height and moves the monitor.

The scene is repeated from multiple angles, ending with the man sitting in a chair and the desk at its lowest height. The desk can be raised with a single hand, with an illuminated button, and moved forward from the back.

The man sits and types as well as holds a mouse and a smartphone. Then, the desk returns to its original height, and we see the top of the tower and a partially raised and then lowered desk.

The man begins sitting in his chair again at the desk, with cup and smartphone on the desk, as the room is shown in bright light with natural light from a window. We see the monitor displaying an image of a green plant in a red plant holder.

summary.brief: A man assembles, adjusts, and works at a height‑adjustable wooden desk with a floating ultrawide monitor.
summary.detailed: The video opens with animated titles and a view of a wooden desk topped by a floating ultrawide monitor. Hands place a black box on the surface, wipe the tabletop with a white cloth, and arrange a glass of water, a black‑silver keyboard, a mouse, and a cup while a banner advertises the IKEA Karlby top. The desk is pulled out and pushed back several times as the presenter, David, sits, stands, and briefly uses a yellow foam roller for a stretch. He repeatedly presses an illuminated button to raise or lower the desk, slides the monitor to a comfortable height and angle, and adjusts his ergonomic chair. While the desk is at different heights he types on a Logitech K810 keyboard, clicks a Logitech G602 mouse, holds a smartphone, and watches the monitor display a static image of a green plant in a red pot. Later he unplugs a cable from the monitor, scrolls with the mouse, and presses a foot‑activated button on the computer tower. The room is bright with natural light from a window, white‑framed pictures on the walls, and the desk legs move visibly. The segment ends with the desk returned to its lowest setting, David seated in the chair, the plant image still on the monitor, and the workspace illuminated by daylight.

action.detailed: Press the illuminated button to raise or lower the wooden desk, slide the floating monitor into place, sit in the ergonomic chair, place your hands on the keyboard and mouse, type, and use the smartphone as needed while the desk moves.

You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to any of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   - "navigation": the camera moves through a physical environment as an
     agent traverses space — first-person walking tours (museum, store,
     home, city street), driving / cycling / hiking POV footage, drone
     fly-throughs of indoor or outdoor scenes, room/house walkthroughs.
     The camera's translation through the environment IS the main content.
     Does NOT count: a stationary tripod with someone talking; a tutorial
     filmed in one place; b-roll where the camera only pans or zooms but
     does not translate; sports footage where the player moves but the
     camera stays put.
   A video can match zero, one, or multiple domains. Be strict — when in
   doubt, say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
